name: Array Element-wise Assignment
description: How a = b + c on rank-1 arrays flows from HLFIR elemental through to a counted loop in LLVM IR
source:
subroutine array_add(a, b, c, n)
  implicit none
  integer, intent(in)  :: n
  real,    intent(in)  :: b(n), c(n)
  real,    intent(out) :: a(n)

  ! This single line triggers the full elemental lowering chain
  a = b + c

end subroutine array_add

  %n_ext = sext i32 %n_val to i64, !dbg !10

loop:                                        ; preds = %loop.preheader, %loop

  %exit   = icmp eq i64 %iv.next, %n_ext, !dbg !12
  br i1 %exit, label %return, label %loop, !dbg !12

return:                                      ; preds = %loop, %entry
  ret void, !dbg !13
}

correlations.lowering_notes: Array assignment lowers through HLFIR's elemental model: hlfir.elemental captures the element-wise semantics as a value-typed expression (!hlfir.expr), then lowered to fir.do_loop + fir.array_fetch/update, finally becoming a counted loop in LLVM IR with GEP + load + fadd + store.

lowering_patterns.name: Elemental Array Operation
lowering_patterns.description: Source-level array operator → hlfir.elemental (value semantics) → fir.do_loop (loop materialization) → LLVM counted loop with GEP

lowering_patterns.name: Array Merge Store
lowering_patterns.description: fir.array_merge_store is the final step that writes the loop result back to the dummy argument's memory location, respecting Fortran's copy-in/copy-out semantics
